content.title: About
content.content: Beef lung is an organ meat from cattle, with a light, spongy, mildly flavored flesh. It is traditionally eaten in several cuisines, including Central Asian, Eastern European, and Middle Eastern dishes, where it is boiled, stewed, or used in sausages and fillings. Its sale for human consumption is restricted or banned in some countries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef lung has a light, spongy texture and a mild flavor.
It is used in traditional dishes in Central Asia, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, and elsewhere.
Lung is lower in fat than many other organ meats.
In some countries, such as the United States, the sale of lung for human food is prohibited for food safety reasons.
Lung must be thoroughly cleaned and boiled, and it is usually cooked for a long time.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Beef lung provides protein with relatively little fat.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Beef lung contains iron, which supports oxygen transport.

items.title: Provides vitamin C
items.content: Unlike most meats, lung contains some vitamin C.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12 and copper
items.content: These nutrients support red blood cell formation and metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Lung is lean compared with many other cuts.

items.title: Legal restrictions and food safety
items.content: Lung can contain fluids and contaminants from the airways and stomach, which is why it is banned in some countries. Buy it only from a source permitted by local regulations.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Lung spoils quickly and must be very fresh and cooked thoroughly, to at least about 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Cholesterol and purines
items.content: Lung contains cholesterol and purines, which matters for people with certain conditions such as gout.

items.title: Contaminants
items.content: Organs can accumulate environmental contaminants, so eat lung in moderation and choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beef lung is usually thoroughly rinsed, boiled for a long time until firm, then sliced and fried, stewed, or added to soups, fillings, and sausages. It is often cooked with onions, spices, and herbs to improve its flavor. Where it is legal, buy it only from a reliable, regulated source.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Beef lung is highly perishable. Keep it refrigerated and cook it within a day, or freeze it for longer storage. Cooked lung should be refrigerated in an airtight container and eaten within a day or two. Discard any lung that smells off.
